key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even with deep gap states, defect-assisted recombination is strongly suppressed and is unlikely to explain the observed efficiency limits.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, with defect management needs that are less severe than in many competing materials.
method: First-principles calculations of point defects in trigonal selenium
Evaluation of Shockley-Read-Hall recombination via nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture
Analysis across a large, chemically diverse defect set under varying defect levels, charge states, and doping conditions
evidence_signal: The study reports large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per recombination event, which strongly suppress defect-mediated SRH losses in the calculated dataset.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on theoretical defect calculations, so real-device performance can still depend on defect concentrations, microstructure, contacts, and processing-induced imperfections not fully captured here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
